theoryOfChange: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) describes its 'People x Biology x Data' strategy as an 'innovative framework' that accelerates the pace of discovery and ensures new insights are translated into effective therapies for patients. This framework, detailed in their 'Our Impact' section and Annual Impact Reports, emphasizes the integration of bioinformatics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to advance cancer immunotherapy. CRI states that this approach transforms funding into discovery and ideas into therapies, creating an ecosystem where innovation thrives.

rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1953, the Cancer Research Institute (CRI) funds clinician-scientists developing novel immunotherapies for cancer patients. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $23,964,638</cite>, representing a decline from $32,295,259 in FY2023. CRI maintains a <cite id="2">94/100 overall rating from Charity Navigator</cite> and allocates resources heavily toward direct grantmaking for research initiatives. In FY2023, the organization distributed <cite id="3">$76,087,418 in total research grants</cite> across domestic and foreign institutions. The organization holds a <cite id="4">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite> and maintains substantial financial reserves. However, executive compensation and board oversight represent areas requiring scrutiny, with CEO compensation reaching <cite id="1">$539,137 in FY2023</cite>, accounting for 2.2% of annual revenue. CRI operates with <cite id="2">21.2 months of working capital</cite>, providing strong short-term liquidity alongside a low fundraising cost structure of $0.11 per $1 raised.
